result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 393–394). I didn't add a new test or run any mock-path cases through the rules, so the new behaviour is untested. The `Scop*Test*` tests in `codeanalyzer` ran with no failures. That pattern may not have matched any test class, though, and I didn't check.

- **Old rules:** `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`. They needed at least one extra character from a small ASCII set after `mock`, so plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and `mock模拟/` all slipped through.
- **New rules:** `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`. Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now matches, whatever follows. The match stops at the next `/`, so it can't span into other folders.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already normalizes backslashes to `/` before matching, so Windows-style paths work without further changes.
- **Cases that should not match:** `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`. The pattern needs `/mock` at the start of a folder name followed by a `/` later in the path.
- **Cases that should still match:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/`.

The patterns still need a `/` before `mock`, as before, so a path that begins directly with `mock/` and has no parent folder isn't caught.
